item.title: Weighted Fourier capacities and Frostman restriction estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.20800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a weighted Fourier capacity attached to compact sets, $ c_{p,k}(K)=\inf\left\{\|k\widehat u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)}:u\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d),\ u\geq 1 \text{ on } K\right\},$ where $k$ is a positive tempered weight. The paper develops complementary upper and lower estimates for this quantity. The upper bounds are obtained from Frostman data, Fourier restriction estimates, and Bessel-potential majorants, which together provide admissible smooth majorants of the compact set. The lower bounds follow from a dual testing argument against positive measures supported on $K$, yielding estimates in terms of the weighted $L^{p'}$ size of their Fourier transforms. For sets of positive Lebesgue measure, testing with $\chi_K\,\mathrm{d}x$ connects the capacity with the weighted integrability of $\widehat{\chi_K}$. A Lebedev-type Sobolev criterion then gives non-triviality ranges governed by the upper Minkowski dimension of $\partial K$ and the growth of the weight. We also record consequences for Ahlfors-David regular sets and positive-measure Cantor-type examples.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Leon, Vicente Vergara

item.title: The $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with degenerate curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.20909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ proved by the first author in \cite{Be-6} and refine the result in the case when the curvature assumptions contain small parameters. The standard $L^p$ estimate is replaced by a more complex norm/quasi-norm of type $\ell^p L^\frac{2}{n-2}$ which reflects the geometry of wave packet propagation and the degenerate curvature assumptions. The primary motivation for this work stems from a concrete application to the study of the quadratic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$, which is done in a companion paper \cite{BeBoCh}.
item.dc:creator: Ioan Bejenaru, Tiklung Chan

item.title: Fourier decay and endpoint estimates for lacunary maximal operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.21197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study endpoint estimates for lacunary maximal operators associated with compactly supported measures. For every $d\geq1$, we construct a compactly supported, absolutely continuous probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ with polynomial Fourier decay whose associated lacunary maximal operator fails to map $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ boundedly into $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. In particular, it fails to be of weak type $(1,1)$. This gives a negative answer to the weak type $(1,1)$ question posed by Seeger and Wright in 2011 and to Open Problems 14 and 15, contributed by Wright at the 2016 Conference in Harmonic Analysis, held at the University of Wisconsin--Madison in honor of Professor Michael Christ.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojing Zhou

item.title: Functions of bounded variation are not dense in the Strong BD Norm
item.description: arXiv:2610.21343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that functions of bounded variation are not dense in the space of functions of bounded deformation with respect to the strong BD norm. Using alternating Riesz products and directional slicing, we construct on every nonempty open subset of $\R^n$ ($n\ge2$) a continuous, compactly supported BD function that is at positive distance from BV.
item.dc:creator: Panu Lahti, Quoc-Hung Nguyen

item.title: B\'ezout bounds and rational points on quasianalytic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For functions $f : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $\mathcal C_M$, we establish explicit bounds for the number of intersection points of the graph $\Gamma(f)$ with algebraic curves of degree at most $d$. The bounds are given in terms of the Bang degree determined by the weight sequence $M$, the degree $d$, and the norming constant of $\Gamma(f)$ with respect to the space of real bivariate polynomials of degree at most $d$. We give instances, where the bounds are at most polynomial in $d$ and, consequently, the graph $\Gamma(f)$ contains few rational points: the number of rational points of height at most $H$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\log H$.
item.dc:creator: Armin Rainer

item.title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. We show that for the affine fractal percolation $E$, conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, almost surely the dimension of the visible part is equal to $\min\{1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ from all directions except for the major contracting direction. The visible part from the major contracting direction is notably different from the other directions, and we provide a formula for its Hausdorff and box dimensions. In addition, we show that almost surely conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, $\dim_{\rm H} \pi(E) =\min\{ 1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ for every orthogonal projection $\pi$ excluding the one onto the major contracting direction, and given $\dim_{\rm H} E >1$, these projections contain intervals.
item.dc:creator: Eeva Kuure, Markus Myllyoja, Aleksi Py\"or\"al\"a

item.title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
item.description: arXiv:2610.21847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $3.33606$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a convex entropy identity; local elliptic regularity identifies the extension to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.
item.dc:creator: Bo Li, Ji Li, Jinxia Li

item.title: Tauberian rates and the Baire property of ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.21889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Tauberian conditions on the successive differences of real sequences which ensure that: (i) ordinary convergence coincides with ideal convergence; or (ii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal cluster point; or (iii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal limit point. First, we prove that an ideal $\mathcal{I}$ has the Baire property if and only if there exists a positive sequence $(r_n)$ tending to zero, with $\sum_n r_n=\infty$, such that $$ |x_{n+1}-x_n|=O(r_n) $$ is a Tauberian condition for any of the three previous statements. Second, for analytic $P$-ideals, we characterize the validity of the Tauberian rate $O(1/n)$ in terms of properties of lower semicontinuous submeasures which represent it. Lastly, in the case of statistical limit points, we prove that $o(1/n)$ is a Tauberian condition for the statement (iii), whereas $O(1/n)$ need not suffice: in this sense, $o(1/n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for (iii). On the other hand, for statistical cluster points in (ii), $O(1/n)$ is an optimal one among nonincreasing rates. For every positive null sequence $(r_n)$ with divergent sum, we also construct a summable ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $o(r_n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for both statements (ii) and (iii).
item.dc:creator: Paolo Leonetti

item.title: A quantitative form of the planar Falconer distance theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.22222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a quantitative planar form of a multiscale argument for Falconer's distance problem. For every $0<\eta<1$, we obtain a positive lower bound for the Lebesgue measure of the distance set of a compact subset of the unit ball supporting a probability measure with $\nu(B(x,r))\le 2r^{1+\eta}$. The bound depends only on $\eta$. For a compact set of diameter $D$ carrying a probability measure with $\mu(B(x,r))\le A(r/D)^{1+\varepsilon}$, localization gives $|\Delta E|\ge c_{\varepsilon,p}DA^{-p}$ for every fixed $p>1/\varepsilon$. In particular, compact planar sets of Hausdorff dimension greater than one have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure. The proof develops the multiscale method of the September 2026 manuscript of OpenAI, using one sequence of restricted distance measures for both the mass and Fourier estimates. A reconstruction lemma combines summable total-variation errors with summable squared Fourier norms. No endpoint or sharpness assertion is made.
item.dc:creator: Guozheng Cheng, Xiang Fang, Menghan Li, Hongdou Qu, Chengbo Xiao

item.title: Seven Limit Cycles in a Periodically Forced Three-Zone Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a seven-cycle example for a periodically forced scalar equation with a continuous three-zone piecewise-linear nonlinearity. Symbolic integration and linear elimination reduce the four-flight matching conditions to two equations in the residence times. The competing exterior visits produce an additional turn of the critical response and lead to the rational parameters $(A,B,\mu)=(9,3/2,181363/100000)$. At these parameters, finite Taylor estimates give three sign changes of the return displacement. Scalar order, analyticity along transverse itineraries, and half-period reflection then establish at least seven distinct isolated periodic orbits on the phase cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Chaoyu Hu, Jizheng Chen

item.title: Optimization of a Perturbed Implicit Sweeping Process by Constrained Discontinuous Controls
item.description: arXiv:2610.21384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies optimal control problems governed by an implicit sweeping process with velocity-dependent constraint geometry, where the dynamics are described by a differential inclusion involving the normal cone to a moving convex polyhedral set. Such systems form a challenging class of nonsmooth differential inclusions due to the implicit coupling between the state, velocity, and constraint reaction. To address these difficulties, we use a method of discrete approximations together with tools of variational analysis and generalized differentiation. This approach allows us to derive necessary optimality conditions for local minimizer in discrete-time problems and subsequently pass to the limit to obtain optimality conditions for the original continuous-time system. The obtained results extend existing optimal control theory for sweeping processes to a class of implicit dynamical systems with state-and velocity-dependent constraints.
item.dc:creator: Yen Dang, Boris S. Mordukhovich, Dao Nguyen

item.title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.22013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $\pi/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $\pi/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijovi\'c, et al. (1999).
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch

item.title: Reverse square function estimates for degenerate curves and their applications
item.description: arXiv:2602.03167v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building on the classical work of C\'{o}rdoba--Fefferman and the recent work of Schippa, we establish $L^4$ reverse square function estimates for functions whose Fourier support is contained in a $\delta$-neighborhood of the curve $\{(\xi,|\xi|^a): |\xi|\leq 1\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, for all exponents $a\in(0,\infty)\backslash\{1\}$. As applications, we derive sharp $L^4$ Strichartz estimates on the one-dimensional torus for fractional Schr\"{o}dinger equations and establish new local smoothing estimates in modulation spaces. In the latter application, orthogonal Strichartz-type estimates also play a crucial role.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandar Bulj, Kotaro Inami, Shobu Shiraki

item.title: Transversal H\"older Criteria and Dini--Zygmund Endpoint Regularity for Hyperbolic Harmonic Mappings
item.description: arXiv:2608.13927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n\ge3$, and let $u$ be a bounded hyperbolic harmonic mapping on the real hyperbolic upper half-space $\mathbb H^n$. First, for $0<\alpha<1$, we establish quantitative transversal and modulus criteria for the global $\alpha$-H\"older continuity of $u$. Then, we construct lacunary examples to show that these criteria are invalid when $\alpha=1$. Finally, under additional integral conditions, we obtain the corresponding global Lipschitz continuity and give Dini--Zygmund conditions on the boundary trace that ensure the Lipschitz continuity.
item.dc:creator: Suling Tan, Hong-Ping Li

item.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20385v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional Gaussian discrepancy, defined as $$\mathcal D(\mu):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}\mu}|G_R^\mu(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^\mu(x):=(4\pi R^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,d\mu(z)$. Provided that $\mu$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\le\delta<\infty$, the so-called width of $\mu$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}\mu\subseteq \bar B_\delta(V+x_0),\quad \delta^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(\mu),$$ where $\bar B_\delta(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(\mu)=0$, the support of $\mu$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $\mu$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $\mu$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Pigati

item.title: Fourier transform of nonlinear images of self-similar measures: qualitative aspects
item.description: arXiv:2606.09743v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The goal of this paper is to establish polynomial Fourier decay for images of self-similar measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^k$ under sufficiently nonlinear real-analytic maps $f \colon \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^d$. For example, we prove that if $f$ is analytic on $\mathbb{R}^k$, its graph does not lie in an affine hyperplane in $\mathbb{R}^{k+d}$, and $\mu$ is not supported in an affine hyperplane in $\mathbb{R}^k$, then the image measure has polynomial Fourier decay. Key steps in the proof include establishing a uniform Lojasiewicz-type inequality for self-similar measures, and using the decay of the Fourier transform of $\mu$ outside a very small exceptional set of frequencies. As an application of our results, we prove polynomial Fourier decay for self-conformal measures on $\mathbb{C}$ for a large class of complex analytic IFSs which are not self-similar but are conjugate to a linear IFS via an analytic map.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Banaji, Han Yu

item.title: Arcsine kernels, inverse-binomial harmonic sums, and classical hypergeometric transformations
item.description: arXiv:2607.09904v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study inverse-central-binomial series with finite reciprocal-square factors and harmonic weights involving $H_n$, $H_{2n}$, and $1/n$. An arcsine integral gives explicit odd-zeta evaluations and a classification of coefficientwise cancellation within a polynomial ansatz. The scalar examples include an evaluation of weight seven and a direct proof of Sun's Conjecture 3.10. An entire generating relation organizes a second family with finite rational coefficient formulas. We then derive that relation, a supplementary generating family, and the complete two-order construction from Bailey's cubic transformation, contiguity, Gauss's quadratic and connection formulas, Euler's transformation, and Clausen's identity. The derivation retains all three infinity branches and resolves the vanishing denominators in the lower contiguous value. A doubling relation with a unique analytic solution and an explicit algebraic identity complete the proof. Thus the evaluations have a proved classical origin; no independent new hypergeometric summation principle is claimed. An application of a known complete-monotonicity property gives strict signs and global Taylor bounds. All endpoint limits, parameter derivatives, and coefficient extractions are justified.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Arbitrarily Fast Quantum Dispersion in Long-Range Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2608.27326v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct the first examples of one-dimensional long-range crystals exhibiting arbitrarily fast polynomial dispersive bounds. The Floquet functions of our Hamiltonians are highly oscillatory Weierstrass functions, whose rough autosimilar structure drives the fast dispersion. The proof develops a new Fourier decay theory for $C^\alpha$ images of the Lebesgue measure, based on a Dolgopyat-inspired transfer operator method, and yields a van der Corput lemma for Weierstrass functions. As a consequence, the local time of classical Weierstrass functions of sufficiently large lacunarity exists and is $C^k$, answering a question raised by Geman and Horowitz in 1980.
item.dc:creator: Ga\'etan Leclerc, Mostafa Sabri, Tuomas Sahlsten

item.title: The strong reproducing kernel thesis for Hankel operators and the Garsia norm
item.description: arXiv:2609.33242v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a bounded operator $T$ on $\mathcal H$, we say that $T$ obeys the strong reproducing kernel thesis (SRKT) if $\|T\|=\sup_k\|Tk\|$, where $k$ ranges over the normalized reproducing kernels in $\mathcal H$. Two problems are posed. One of these is to determine which Hankel operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ obey the SRKT. The other concerns the geometry of the unit ball of $BMO$ with respect to the Garsia norm.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin M. Dyakonov
